sub_scenario.one_line: technical translator: batch replies; live chat only if batched

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the term log and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The chapter queue review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Interpreting assignments, pure live work, go fine; that is a different mode entirely.
Live is a mode, not a threat.
A mode I can enter deliberately.
Someone new shadowed me in the translation desk this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the terminology choices into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The device-manual project went flawlessly because I translated in two-hour sealed sessions and logged terminology decisions in one file.
Sealed sessions plus a term log.
That combination is my entire quality system.
Urgent one-off calls between sessions are absorbable.
Rarity again.
Rarity is the entire question.
I archived last cycle's notes on the chapter queue and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Term consistency is the single metric my agency scores hardest.
The stakes concentrate exactly where switching hurts.
Exactly there.
A vendor call about the term log ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the translation desk checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the terminology choices.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the chapter queue records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The agency chat pilot expected instant replies; toggling between translation and chat, I let two inconsistent term choices ship in one chapter.
The log could not save you mid-toggle?
I stopped consulting it; there was no time between pings.
I sketched next week's plan for the terminology choices before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the term log updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I already answer all client queries daily at 14:00 in one batch, and clients have never complained.
A working alternative exists.
Documented and running.
I compared two options for the chapter queue tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the translation desk handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
A new agency asks how I prefer to handle client communication while translating. What should I tell them my track record supports?
